passage:
Sunday: Uma asked Mummy, "Can I teach the Class 5 kids in our lane after school? Their parents offered a small fee." Alka thought for a moment. "One hour, four days a week, and only after your own homework. I will talk to their parents first."

Two weeks later, Wednesday: Uma sat on the veranda with three children, a slate and a bag of chalk. She noted their trouble spots: fractions, spellings. By evening she was tired, but proud.

End of the month: Uma counted the fees on the table: six hundred rupees. She put half in Mummy's hand, "for the house," and half into a tin labelled Exam Fee. Alka pressed her hand and said nothing.

qa.q: How many days a week and how long each day did Alka allow Uma to teach?
qa.a: Alka allowed one hour, four days a week.

qa.q: How did Uma feel on the first Wednesday evening?
qa.a: Uma felt tired but proud after teaching three children.

qa.q: What else could Uma do to keep the earning study-safe, and why?
qa.a: Uma could set a fixed stopping time and skip the sessions in exam week, because study time protects the longer-term goal that the fee is meant for.

qa.q: How might Alka feel when Uma puts half the fees in her hand?
qa.a: Alka is probably moved and proud, which is why she presses Uma's hand and says nothing.

grounding: With parental permission the teen teaches Class 5 children after school for a small fee, keeps it modest and study-safe, and gives part to the household while saving part for exam fees.
